_meta.label: OUR SIMULATION — NOT FROM ORIGINAL PAPERS
_meta.description: Precomputed accuracy-vs-KV-cache-budget sweep for the interactive demo. These numbers are produced by our own project simulation pipeline (a synthetic/representative long-context QA + passkey-retrieval evaluation), not extracted or reproduced from the H2O, SnapKV, StreamingLLM, Quest, or KVzip papers.
_meta.task: synthetic long-context QA + passkey retrieval, avg over multiple context lengths (8K-32K tokens)
_meta.budget_definition: KV cache budget = % of full-context tokens retained (Full Cache = 100%)
_meta.accuracy_definition: task accuracy (%) relative to Full Cache baseline
_meta.note: Use this file for the interactive demo chart. For BDH/BDH-GPU comparisons, use bdh_published_claims.json instead — those figures come from the original paper and are explicitly not reproduced by us.

full_cache.notes: Baseline. Only defined at 100% budget; retains every token's KV pair.

sliding_window.notes: Keeps only the most recent tokens. Degrades sharply on tasks needing information from early/middle context, since there is no sink or importance mechanism.

h2o.notes: Cumulative attention-score-based eviction of heavy hitters + recent tokens. Strong at low-to-mid budgets; slight recency bias shows up as a small accuracy dip vs. SnapKV at very low budgets in our sweep.

snapkv.notes: Prompt-side observation-window voting, selected once at prefill. Performs best of the eviction methods at low budgets in our simulation, consistent with the paper's reported efficiency gains.

streamingllm.notes: Fixed attention-sink tokens + recent window. Stable for generation coherence but weakest on tasks requiring retrieval of specific mid-context facts, matching the qualitative pattern reported in Quest's passkey-retrieval comparison.
